article.summary: Continuous Claude combines Claude Code hooks, continuity artifacts, agent workflows, code analysis, and cross-session memory. Its PostgreSQL learning path stores typed, embedded archival records and recalls them through prompt-time context; source inspection found the factory's default SQLite implementation path absent at this revision and a standalone recall query without session/project filtering. This review ran no runtime, tests, or benchmarks.

who_what.text: The curated roster identifies ordinal 152 as Continuous Claude, slug continuous-claude, with an explicit repository locator; Atlas is retained only as roster attribution.
GitHub identifies main as the default branch; its repository page and main commits feed show current head d07ff4b06b62f43771bc0c927d0211b734d6149e.
The README describes a Claude Code environment with background learning extraction, prompt-time recall, continuity artifacts, hooks, skills, agents, and TLDR code analysis.
The official pinned README was checked for contact; it publishes no contact email.

architecture.text: The overall environment combines Claude Code hooks, skills, agents, continuity ledgers/handoffs, code analysis, and a cross-session memory subsystem.

The PostgreSQL schema separates session coordination, archival learning records, and handoffs. Archival records include UUID, session and optional agent IDs, content, JSON metadata, a 1024-dimensional vector, and creation time; indexes cover session, agent, recency, and full-text content.

The learning writer supports typed records with optional context, tags, and confidence; it embeds content and skips a record when top vector similarity meets 0.85. The memory factory selects PostgreSQL or SQLite, but its SQLite import target is absent at the reviewed head.

behavior.text: Write: a daemon monitors stale sessions and invokes headless Claude to extract learnings from thinking blocks; a CLI also writes typed learnings directly. Daemon source documents 60-second polling, five-minute staleness, a two-process extraction cap, and local-file logging.

Backend: the service factory defaults to SQLite and imports scripts.core.db.memory_service, but that path is absent at this revision. PostgreSQL is implemented in memory_service_pg.py and is selected by configuration or database URL.

Correction/deletion: the inspected archival writer uses vector deduplication rather than a correction/supersession protocol. The reviewed learning recall and write entry points do not expose a forget operation or deletion audit; PostgreSQL core-memory set replaces a key but is a different data path.

Retrieval: README describes hybrid text/vector recall and automatic prompt injection. The standalone PostgreSQL recall query filters to session-learning records but has no session or project predicate, so it can return records across those boundaries.

Scope: archival rows record session and optional agent IDs, and PostgreSQL core-memory operations use session/agent predicates. The inspected standalone recall query does not apply those filters; record scope therefore does not guarantee isolation on every retrieval path.

Provenance: learning rows carry a session identifier and JSON metadata; handoffs separately have optional transcript path and span fields. The archival schema has no dedicated source transcript/evidence-span field, and confidence metadata is not an evidence-verification mechanism.

Efficiency/observability: extraction runs outside the active request path, PostgreSQL provides full-text and vector indexes, and the daemon bounds concurrent extraction and writes a local log. No performance or reliability results were measured.

metrics.evidence: Search paths are present, but no answerability or abstention workload was run.
The reviewed learning writer has deduplication but no inspected correction workload or outcome.
No forget workflow or post-delete retrieval check was run.
The standalone recall query lacks session/project predicates; no cross-session isolation workload was run.
Metadata and handoff trace fields exist, but no support or citation evaluation was run.
Indexes and search code are present; no latency workload was collected.
The daemon polls stale sessions; no indexing or recall delay was measured.
The README makes token-efficiency claims for project components; no memory-specific token or cost results were collected.
The schema defines storage and embeddings; no storage footprint workload was run.

limits.text: The configured default SQLite backend points to an absent source file at the reviewed head; the system was not executed to measure the resulting behavior.
The inspected standalone recall query is not session/project scoped even though archival rows carry session identifiers.
The reviewed writer and recall entry points do not establish a complete correction, forget, deletion-audit, or evidence-validation lifecycle.
This review covers selected current source and README material, not every hook, configuration, migration, or deployment topology.
